title: Cross-stitch lavender sprig
subtitle: Three stems of lavender in purple and grey-green on 14-count white Aida
excerpt: Three spikes of lavender in shades of purple and mauve with grey-green stems and foliage on 14-count white Aida. The design is approximately 45 by 90 stitches and finishes at around 8 by 16 cm. The tall narrow shape suits a vertical frame or a bookmark mount.
sourceNotes: Original design. Lavender (Lavandula angustifolia) is native to the Mediterranean and a traditional British garden plant. Botanical cross-stitch is a well-established category in UK needlework publishing.

content.text: The lavender design uses only five colours and no specialist stitches. The flower spikes are built from individual clusters of cross-stitches worked in three purple tones; the stems and leaves use two grey-green shades. The result is clean and fast for a beginner first project.

items.label: Hoop
items.value: 12 cm embroidery hoop (move as you stitch the tall design)

items.label: Thread
items.value: DMC 210 (medium lavender), 209 (dark lavender), 208 (very dark lavender), 3053 (green grey), 3052 (medium green grey)

content.text: Work each stem as a single vertical column of cross-stitches in 3053 from bottom to the point where the flower spike begins. The three stems are spaced approximately twelve stitches apart.
Add the leaves along each stem.
Work small diagonal pairs of cross-stitches (two per side) in 3052 along the lower third of each stem as the narrow leaf pairs.
Build each flower spike from the base up.

Each spike is roughly oval, wider in the middle than at the tip. Start with 208 (darkest) at the base cluster, move to 209 in the middle section, and use 210 (lightest) at the top two or three stitch clusters.
Work small back-stitch marks in 3053 between the colour clusters to suggest the individual calyx bracts of the lavender floret.
Trim to a 3 cm border on each side and frame in a 10 × 20 cm vertical frame. Alternatively, trim to a long strip, back with ribbon-weight interfacing, and fold the ends to create a bookmark.
